linkedin:
Authentic Product Verified. Counterfeit Alert, with the specific reason the hash didn't check out. Product Found — No Hash Signature, for a registered item whose scan carried no signature to check. Those are the only three outcomes an AuthiChain verification page will ever show — plain language, not a bare pass/fail badge.

Getting there takes nothing extra: scan the signed QR code on an AuthiChain-registered product with your phone's own camera app and it opens authichain.com/verify directly. No separate app to install, no login. The page reads a product ID and a cryptographic hash out of the QR data and checks the hash against the registry on the spot.

Underneath the result sits the product card itself — name, brand, manufacturer, serial number, category, and the date the item was registered — so the person holding the product sees what's actually on file, not just a checkmark.

We think a verification result is only as trustworthy as its honesty about uncertainty — which is why "no signature to check" is its own stated outcome, not folded into a pass.

https://authichain.com/verify?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=consumer-verify-flow&utm_content=b

reddit.title: Three honest outcomes for a product-authenticity scan — not just pass/fail — and how we decided what counts as a third state
reddit.body:
AuthiChain issues signed QR codes for physical products, and every scan lands on one of exactly three plain-language results: Authentic Product Verified, a Counterfeit Alert (with the specific reason the hash didn't check out), or Product Found — No Hash Signature, for items that are registered but the scan didn't carry a signature to verify.

That third state was the harder design call — it would've been simpler to just show pass/fail and quietly treat "no signature" as a fail. We didn't, because collapsing "we couldn't check" into "this failed" misrepresents what actually happened.

Getting to the result takes no extra app: scanning the QR with a phone's own camera opens authichain.com/verify with the product ID and hash encoded in the URL, and below the result sits the actual product record — name, brand, manufacturer, serial number, category, registration date — not just the badge.

Curious how others handle the "we genuinely don't know" case in a customer-facing verification flow — fold it into fail, or give it its own state?

https://authichain.com/verify?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=consumer-verify-flow&utm_content=b

Disclosure: I work on this project.
